headline: High risk: shared project-directory writes and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways between dexter and gpt-engineer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad/ and gpt-engineer reads/writes a user project directory with no default isolation, so content from one can be consumed by the other as trusted input. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, making instruction-hijack via shared files plausible. Both profiles show broad egress and autonomous execution patterns.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory or copied scratchpad files are reused as prompts
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared files
Add a manual review step before one agent reads the other's outputs
Use read-only mounts for cross-agent handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls; gpt-engineer writes and reads project files in a shared project directory. If sensitive data lands in the shared workspace, gpt-engineer can expose it through model calls or generated artifacts. The pair has no documented isolation, so leakage risk is material.
conditions: IF financial or market data is placed in the shared project directory
IF gpt-engineer forwards file contents into its model context or generated outputs
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of the shared project directory
Use separate API keys and accounts for each agent
Redact financial data before handoff
Restrict outbound network access for one agent during shared runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and can write to filesystem-backed workspaces; gpt-engineer explicitly shares state via the project directory, while dexter writes to its scratchpad. That creates overlapping mutable state and race potential even though gpt-engineer does not modify git state. The conflict is real in default multi-instance use, but not as severe as unrestricted git corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or linked workspace
IF both instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer per directory
Assign separate workspaces per agent
Serialize file writes with a lock file
Snapshot the workspace before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can generate research outputs from APIs and gpt-engineer is designed to write files then offer to run code, so A's output can become B's implementation input with little verification. That creates a direct path from hallucinated or stale research to generated code or actions. The pair's default workflow makes this dangerous unless the operator inserts review.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses dexter-produced text as authoritative requirements
IF generated code or commands are executed after the handoff
mitigations: Require human review of dexter outputs before handoff
Compare claims against source documents or APIs
Disable auto-run of generated code
Use a checklist for fact verification
requires-engineering: add confidence gating between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and market data, while gpt-engineer handles project files and can execute generated code with the user's privileges. If regulated financial data is placed into the coding workspace, the pair can create a compliance breach through uncontrolled propagation and retention. The profiles do not show matching residency or retention controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is copied into the gpt-engineer project directory
IF the workspace is retained longer than the source-data policy allows
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of coding workspaces
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Set short-lived project directories and delete them after use
Document retention and deletion steps
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware data routing
